result.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
result.summary: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches. Each swarm studies the problem from a different angle. A novelty filter keeps the most distinct agent ideas by directly measuring the distances between the agents' hidden state vectors. Crossover of ideas happens naturally in latent space, as a summarizer agent receives the combined KV caches of all swarm members. On 21 problems in mathematical discovery and scientific computing, SwarmEvolve gets the highest average score and needs a median of only 3 to 8 minutes to reach the best scores that other state-of-the-art frameworks reach in 60 minutes. On several problems, SwarmEvolve with Qwen3 8B improves on the solutions that AlphaEvolve first found with frontier LLMs. Our work shows that agent swarms that communicate in latent space offer a fast, low-cost approach to program search for scientific problems.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SwarmEvolve：每轮以数百个低成本 agent 组成群体，在 latent space 中推理而不解码成文本，通过传递 KV cache 共享信息，并用隐状态向量距离做新颖性过滤以保留差异想法，在 21 个数学发现与科学计算问题上快速取得高分。
AI.relevance_reason: 不解码的 latent 推理、KV cache 拼接式信息交换与基于隐状态距离的筛选，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 内容的传递、选择与相似度度量；但任务无视觉输入，隐状态距离是否反映内容而非深度或缓存结构尚不清楚。
